entries.title: The Hermetic Arts
entries.summary: Explains that magi have a score in each Technique and Form, that a spell combines one of each, and that a Form score gives a Form Bonus to resist related hazards (bonuses do not stack).
quotes: FORM BONUS: Form score/5 (rounded up)
These bonuses do not stack.

entries.title: Creo
entries.summary: What the Technique Creo can create, heal or improve, why artificial items need an Int + Finesse roll, and how long created things and their effects last.
quotes: An Int + Finesse roll is made to determine how good the created thing is.

entries.title: Intellego
entries.summary: What the Technique Intellego reveals: the true nature of a thing rather than its appearance, so it is not fooled by mundane disguises.
quotes: Thus, Intellego magic is not deceived by mundane disguises.

entries.title: Muto
entries.summary: What the Technique Muto can change: it grants or removes properties but cannot give a target an unnatural property that other things cannot confer, nor directly injure or kill.
quotes: Muto magic cannot affect the properties that something has naturally

entries.title: Perdo
entries.summary: What the Technique Perdo can destroy: it makes things worse examples of their kind, destroys whole properties, and is easier when the thing can naturally lose the property.
quotes: destroying properties that a thing cannot naturally lose falls under the Limit of Essential Nature (see page 210)

related.text: ArM5 p.210 Limit of Essential Nature

entries.title: Rego
entries.summary: What the Technique Rego can do: change a thing to another state it can naturally have, such as moving it, with a Finesse roll to set the quality of crafted outcomes.
quotes: Rego magic allows a maga to move things around

entries.title: Animal
entries.summary: The Form Animal covers animals but not people, and its Form Bonus applies to soak against animal attacks and to resisting animal poisons.
quotes: Animal spells cannot affect people
Form Bonus: Soak against animal attacks (claws, bites, etc.), rolls to resist animal poisons.

entries.title: Aquam
entries.summary: The Form Aquam covers water and liquids, and its Form Bonus helps resist drowning, thirst and water jets.
quotes: Form Bonus: Rolls to resist drowning and thirst, soak against water jets and the like.

entries.title: Auram
entries.summary: The Form Auram covers air, wind, weather and gases, and its Form Bonus helps resist suffocation and weather damage.
quotes: Form bonus: Rolls to resist suffocation, including drowning, soak against weather phenomena such as lightning.

entries.title: Corpus
entries.summary: The Form Corpus covers human bodies, living or dead, and its Form Bonus helps against human unarmed attacks and disease but not aging rolls.
quotes: Form bonus: Soak against human unarmed attacks, rolls to resist disease. It does not apply to aging rolls.

entries.title: Herbam
entries.summary: The Form Herbam covers plants and plant matter, and its Form Bonus helps against wooden weapons, herbal poisons and starvation.
quotes: Form bonus: Soak against wooden weapons, rolls to resist herbal poisons, rolls to resist starvation.

entries.title: Ignem
entries.summary: The Form Ignem covers fire, heat and light, and its Form Bonus helps soak fire and cold.
quotes: Form bonus: Soak against fire and cold.

entries.title: Imaginem
entries.summary: The Form Imaginem covers sensory species; it normally affects how species are produced, can affect species directly (which then must Penetrate), and only changes appearance, not real effects.
quotes: Form bonus: Rolls to resist confusion, deafening, or nausea caused by sights, sounds, smells, or tastes.

related.text: Houses of Hermes: Societates, Jerbiton chapter

entries.title: Mentem
entries.summary: The Form Mentem covers minds, thoughts, spirits and the bodies of noncorporeal beings, and its Form Bonus helps resist mundane persuasion, deception and temptation.
quotes: Form bonus: Rolls to resist mundane persuasion, deception, or temptation.

entries.title: Terram
entries.summary: The Form Terram covers solids, especially earth and stone, and its Form Bonus helps soak metal or stone weapons and resist mineral poisons.
quotes: Form bonus: Soak against metal or stone weapons, rolls to resist mineral poisons.

entries.title: Vim
entries.summary: The Form Vim covers raw magical power and magical, infernal, divine and faerie creatures, and its Form Bonus helps resist Twilight and soak damage from the caster's own spellcasting.
quotes: Form bonus: Rolls to resist Twilight (see page 228), but not rolls to comprehend it

entries.title: The Elemental Forms
entries.summary: Explains how Aquam, Auram, Ignem and Terram overlap on one substance (lava, ice, mist, hail) and when requisites are needed.
quotes: As a rule, simple creation or destruction of a non-living thing needs only the basic Art, without requisites (see page 311).

entries.title: Magic Resistance
entries.summary: Most humans have no Magic Resistance; Hermetic magi have a base resistance equal to the most applicable Form score, and creatures with Might resist with their Might. A target with Magic Resistance 0 is affected only by a Penetration total of 1 or more.
quotes: Hermetic magi have a base Magic Resistance equal to their score in the Form most applicable to the spell cast.
If the target of a spell has Magic Resistance of 0, she is only affected if the Penetration total is 1 or greater.

entries.title: Parma Magica
entries.summary: The Parma Magica Ability adds to Form-based Magic Resistance, takes two minutes to perform and lasts until sunrise or sunset, can be suppressed by concentration, and can protect other people at a cost in effective score.
quotes: Parma Magica adds Magic Resistance equal to five times the maga's score in the Ability to the resistance based on her Forms.
While a magus is protecting others, his effective Parma Magica score is reduced by 3 points

entries.title: Parma Magica
entries.summary: Hermetic protection ritual that adds to Magic Resistance for a time, can be suppressed, can be extended to other people, and shields from the social penalties of other people's Gifts.
quotes: It lets you add 5 times your Parma Magica score to your Magic Resistance until the next sunrise or sunset, whichever comes first.
While a magus is protecting others, his effective Parma Magica score is reduced by 3 points

entries.title: The Functioning of Magic Resistance
entries.summary: How Magic Resistance applies to the caster's own spells, groups, magical and magically moved things, with a long list of worked examples (water jets, rocks, bridges, invisibility, illusions).
quotes: Magic Resistance keeps magic away from the maga, her clothing, and other items that are very close to her. It does not dispel magic.
Spells cast with Personal Range do not have to overcome the caster's own Magic Resistance.

entries.title: Aiming
entries.summary: Indirect spell effects that bypass the victim's Magic Resistance must be aimed with a roll treated as an attack total, with bonuses for larger targets.
quotes: AIMING ROLL: Perception + Finesse + Die
For every step larger, and thus for every magnitude added to the spell, the aiming roll gets a +6 bonus.

entries.title: Magic Resistance and Penetration of Creatures
entries.summary: Creatures with a Might Score derive Magic Resistance and Penetration from it, and characters with non-Hermetic supernatural abilities have their own Penetration formula.
quotes: CREATURE MAGIC RESISTANCE: Might Score + Aura Modifier
CREATURE PENETRATION: Might Score – (5 x Might Points spent on power) + Penetration Bonus + Aura Modifier
CHARACTER PENETRATION: Effect Roll – Ease Factor + Penetration Bonus + Aura Modifier

entries.title: Awareness of Attack
entries.summary: A target whose Magic Resistance stops a spell knows an effect was stopped but nothing about it; a penetrating spell gives no warning beyond its obvious effects.
quotes: If a spell is stopped by Magic Resistance, the target knows that some effect has been stopped, but knows nothing about it.

entries.title: Bypassing Magic Resistance
entries.summary: Examples of spells that harm the victim indirectly and so bypass Magic Resistance but must be aimed.
quotes: The following are examples of spells that bypass the ultimate victim's Magic Resistance, and thus need to be aimed.

entries.title: Projectiles and Rego Magic
entries.summary: Three ways Rego magic can be used offensively with projectiles: propelled entirely by magic (resisted, no aiming), natural motion such as dropping a rock (aimed, bypasses resistance), and a jolt of force that launches a projectile (aimed, bypasses resistance, range increment 20 paces).
quotes: Spells that throw a projectile release control of it immediately after launching it.
Most projectiles thrown by spells have a range increment of 20 paces.

entries.title: Learning Parma Magica
entries.summary: An apprentice accumulates Parma Magica experience through exposure but cannot invoke it until the final key instruction is given after swearing the Oath of Hermes; teaching it earlier is a High Crime.
quotes: Usually, an apprentice character finishes apprenticeship with a score of 1 in Parma Magica.
doing so before the apprentice swears the Oath of Hermes is a High Crime

entries.title: Protections Against Magic for Mundane Characters
entries.summary: Ways a mundane character can be shielded from magic: a relic giving Magic Resistance, a Guardian Angel, or effective folk charms. Five sample charms each give a roll, Ease Factor or bonus against a specific kind of ongoing magical effect.
quotes: Sir Erwan may have a Guardian Angel (which gives him a magic resistance of 15
gives Sir Erwan a +3 Soak bonus against magic sources of damage

entries.title: Penetration Total
entries.summary: Excess casting total over spell level, plus Penetration Bonus, is used to overcome Magic Resistance; a zero or negative total cannot affect any target with Magic Resistance.
quotes: PENETRATION TOTAL: Casting Total + Penetration Bonus - Spell Level

entries.title: Arcane Connections
entries.summary: An Arcane Connection lets a maga target something she is not sensing, if the spell has Arcane Connection range; connections fade over a time that depends on the item, as listed in the table.
quotes: Arcane Connections allow a maga to cast a spell on something she is not currently sensing, as long as she is currently aware of the Arcane Connection.

entries.title: Penetration
entries.summary: Penetration lets a spell affect targets with Magic Resistance; characters with the Penetration Ability can multiply it using an Arcane Connection and other sympathetic connections.
quotes: The Penetration Bonus starts at one times the character's Penetration Ability, and the multiplier can be increased.

entries.title: Enhancing Spell Penetration
entries.summary: Practical advice for overcoming high Magic Resistance: favor low-level spells, improve Penetration, use Spell Mastery, and add Arcane and sympathetic connections.
quotes: so if one has both a name and a picture of one's target, the multiplier would be x4

related.text: ArM5 p.84 Arcane and sympathetic connections

entries.title: Forceless Casting
entries.summary: A maga may deliberately cast so that her Penetration Total is 0, avoiding affecting magi with Magic Resistance 0, useful in tournaments and area spells.
quotes: A maga can deliberately ensure the Penetration Total of a spell does not exceed 0.

entries.title: Sympathetic Connections
entries.summary: Table of sympathetic connections (blood relative, signature, names, horoscopes, symbolic representations) and the bonus each gives to the Penetration multiplier, with the rolls needed to cast horoscopes or make representations.
quotes: succeed in an Int + Artes Liberales (Astronomy) roll against an Ease Factor of 9
a Dexterity + Craft roll of 9+ to create

entries.title: Penetration Example
entries.summary: Worked example of building a high Penetration with an Arcane Connection, a daily horoscope and Penetration Mastery.
quotes: This gives her a bonus of +4 to the Penetration multiplier

entries.title: Art as an Arcane Connection
entries.summary: An original piece of artwork acts as an Arcane Connection to its creator for a limited time that depends on how long it took to make, shortened by assistants, while copies and very large works do not count. Performances need Imaginem magic to capture, and the connection can be fixed like any other.
quotes: a piece of art maintains an Arcane Connection to its creator for a length of time equal to half the time it took to create it
Subtract one week from the length of time an Arcane Connection lasts for every assistant the creating artist had.

entries.title: Craftsman's Stamp (Arcane Connection and Forgery)
entries.summary: A craftsman's stamp on his goods acts as an Arcane Connection to him for a duration depending on how long the item took to make, and the stamp can be forged or altered by magic or skill.
quotes: A stamped good serves as an Arcane Connection to the crafter
this requires a Finesse roll against an Ease Factor of 18

entries.title: Penetrating Cold (Penetration of Created Weather)
entries.summary: Clarifies which weather and cold effects must Penetrate: magically created media or controlled substances must, while mundane items moved by magic and then released need not.
quotes: Magically created media or magically controlled substances must Penetrate, but mundane items that have been moved by magic and then released need not.

entries.title: Casting Spells
entries.summary: Defines the Casting Score used for all spellcasting and notes that the Casting Total is computed differently per spell type and a botch makes it zero.
quotes: CASTING SCORE: Technique + Form + Stamina - Encumbrance + Aura Modifier
If the casting roll botches, the casting total is treated as zero, in addition to any other effects.

entries.title: Spell Basics
entries.summary: Every Hermetic spell has a Technique, Form and Level, and a magnitude derived from the level.
quotes: Spells also have a magnitude, which is equal to the level divided by five, rounded up.

entries.title: Formulaic Magic
entries.summary: Casting a known spell: add a die to the Casting Score and compare to the spell level, with Fatigue lost if the total falls short and failure if it falls short by more than ten; mastered spells always use a stress die with no botch dice when calm.
quotes: FORMULAIC CASTING TOTAL: Casting Score + Die Roll
If the casting total falls short of the spell level by ten or less, the spell takes effect and the maga loses a Fatigue level.

entries.title: Ritual Magic
entries.summary: Ritual spells take fifteen minutes and one pawn of vis per magnitude, add Artes Liberales and Philosophiae to the total, always use a stress die, and cost long-term Fatigue levels (with wounds if she runs out).
quotes: RITUAL CASTING TOTAL: Casting Score + Artes Liberales + Philosophiae + Stress Die
It takes fifteen minutes per magnitude to cast a Ritual spell, and the maga must expend one pawn of vis per magnitude of the spell.

entries.title: Spontaneous Magic
entries.summary: Casting an effect not already known as a spell, either fatiguing or non-fatiguing, with the casting total divided accordingly; the maga may devote surplus total to Range, Duration, Target or Penetration.
quotes: FATIGUING SPONTANEOUS MAGIC CASTING TOTAL: (Casting Score + Stress Die)/2
NON-FATIGUING SPONTANEOUS MAGIC CASTING TOTAL: Casting Score/5

entries.title: Concentration
entries.summary: A maga distracted while casting or maintaining a spell must pass a concentration roll against an Ease Factor set by the distraction, which is reduced by three for maintained spells and has its own table for actions possible only while maintaining.
quotes: CONCENTRATION ROLL: Stamina + Concentration + Stress Die
you must make a concentration roll every two minutes (Diameter duration)

entries.title: Words and Gestures
entries.summary: Option to cast more subtly or more loudly, trading a penalty or bonus to the Casting Score for voice and gesture levels, which also change the range of Voice-range spells.
quotes: using exaggerated gestures but making no noise gives a total penalty of –9 to the casting score.

entries.title: Fast Casting
entries.summary: Casting a Spontaneous spell as an instant response: roll Fast Casting Speed against the opponent's Initiative Total, with a casting penalty and extra botch dice, and work out the attacker's Form to defend.
quotes: FAST CASTING SPEED: Quickness + Finesse + Stress Die
FAST CAST PENALTY: -10 to Casting Score
DETERMINING FORM OF MAGICAL EFFECT: Perception + Awareness vs. 15

entries.title: Ceremonial Casting
entries.summary: A spontaneous casting option that spends time per magnitude to add Artes Liberales and Philosophiae, limiting the spell level to the time spent, with further bonuses for ceremonial props and faster casting in prepared spaces.
quotes: CEREMONIAL CASTING BONUS: Add Artes Liberales and Philosophiae to Casting Score
to one magnitude per fifteen minutes

alsoIn.title: Ceremonial Magic: Props and Prepared Spaces

entries.title: Raw Vis
entries.summary: Explains raw vis as magical power stored in matter associated with one Art, measured in pawns, rooks and queens, and its uses in spells, rituals, enchantment and study.
quotes: Ten pawns are said to make a rook, while ten rooks make a queen.

entries.title: Using Raw Vis
entries.summary: Pawns of vis matching the Technique or Form add to the Casting Score for any spell, up to the maga's score in that Art, at the cost of extra botch dice.
quotes: VIS BOOST TO CASTING SCORE: +2 Casting Score Per Pawn
VIS BOTCH DICE: +1 botch die per pawn of vis used
LIMIT ON VIS USE IN SPELL CASTING: The Maga's Score in the Art of the Vis

entries.title: Detecting vis without supernatural means: Perception
entries.summary: A character without supernatural senses can pick the objects most likely to hold vis from a collection using Perception and a Theory or Magic Lore Ability; the result is only a guess until the vis is used.
quotes: make a Perception + (Hedge Magic) Theory or Magic Lore roll against an Ease Factor of 12

entries.title: Detecting vis without supernatural means: Intelligence
entries.summary: A character can reason about where vis is likely to be found (for example, the first fruit of the season) with an Intelligence roll; finding it remains trial and error.
quotes: make a roll for the character of Intelligence + (Hedge Magic) Theory or Magic Lore against an Ease Factor of 15

entries.title: Lesser Enchantment Vis and Spell-Like Vis
entries.summary: Reminder sidebar on two special kinds of vis: Lesser Enchantment Vis keeps a standing enchantment while unused, and Spell-Like Vis fires one spell (possibly a ritual) and is then expended.
quotes: Lesser Enchantment Vis emulates a Lesser Enchantment, usually of level 30 or less.
Spell-Like Vis has a single use only, mimicking the effects of a spell of up to 60th level

entries.title: Limits of Magic
entries.summary: Introduces the limits Hermetic magic can never exceed: two fundamental limits (the Divine and Essential Nature) and several lesser ones.
quotes: Most Hermetic theorists believe that there are only two fundamental limits

entries.title: The Limit of the Divine
entries.summary: Hermetic magic cannot affect the Divine, though beings with a will separate from God's can in principle be affected.
quotes: Hermetic magic cannot affect the Divine.

entries.title: The Limit of Essential Nature
entries.summary: Magic that violates a thing's essential nature must be maintained, and a thing's essential nature cannot be changed; physical features count as either injuries or essential nature, and Flaw-bought disabilities are essential.
quotes: Any magic which violates a thing's essential nature must be maintained

entries.title: The Lesser Limits
entries.summary: Introduces the list of lesser limits of Hermetic magic that follow.
quotes: The Lesser Limits are as follows.

entries.title: The Limit of Aging
entries.summary: Hermetic magic cannot halt or reverse natural aging or remove Decrepitude, only slow it or mitigate its effects.
quotes: Hermetic magic cannot halt or reverse natural aging, although it can slow it down and mitigate its effects.

entries.title: The Limit of Arcane Connections
entries.summary: Hermetic magic cannot affect an unsensed target without an Arcane Connection, though Intellego is less tightly bound.
quotes: Hermetic magic cannot affect an unsensed target without an Arcane Connection.

entries.title: The Limit of Creation
entries.summary: Creo cannot create anything permanently without raw vis, and a Creo effect with a Muto requisite cannot be made permanent with vis.
quotes: Hermetic magic is incapable of creating anything permanently without raw vis.

entries.title: The Limit of Energy
entries.summary: Hermetic magic cannot restore Fatigue levels or Confidence.
quotes: Hermetic magic cannot restore one's physical energy (Fatigue levels), nor can it restore Confidence

entries.title: The Limit of Experience
entries.summary: Hermetic magic cannot create or transfer skills or knowledge (Abilities) by manipulating minds.
quotes: Hermetic magic cannot create skills or knowledge in a person by manipulating their mind

entries.title: The Limit of the Infernal
entries.summary: Intellego magic is almost useless against the Infernal because it reveals only what demons want believed.
quotes: Intellego magic is almost completely useless against the Infernal

entries.title: The Limit of the Lunar Sphere
entries.summary: Hermetic magic cannot affect the lunar sphere or anything above it.
quotes: Hermetic magic cannot affect the lunar sphere, nor anything above it.

entries.title: The Limit of the Soul
entries.summary: Hermetic magic cannot create an immortal soul, so it cannot create true human life or raise the dead; animals can be created.
quotes: Hermetic magic cannot create an immortal soul

entries.title: The Limit of Time
entries.summary: Hermetic magic cannot alter the passage of time, affect the past, or scry on the past or future.
quotes: Hermetic magic is incapable of altering the passage of time.

entries.title: The Limit of True Feeling
entries.summary: A few humans have a love, friendship or faith Hermetic magic cannot affect, represented by a Virtue or Flaw.
quotes: A few humans have a love, friendship, or faith that Hermetic magic cannot affect in any way.

entries.title: The Limit of Vis
entries.summary: Hermetic magic cannot change the Art to which raw vis is attuned.
quotes: Hermetic magic cannot change the Art to which raw vis is attuned.

entries.title: The Limit of Warping
entries.summary: Hermetic magic cannot undo warping caused by prolonged exposure to active magic or high auras, including Wizard's Twilight.
quotes: Hermetic magic is completely unable to affect these changes once they have happened.

entries.title: The Limit of Magic Resistance
entries.summary: Non-Hermetic magic (and Faerie powers) cannot grant general Magic Resistance, though Divine and Infernal can; some non-Hermetic traditions break other Lesser Limits.
quotes: Non-Hermetic magic is incapable of granting general Magic Resistance

entries.title: The Vital Faculty and Hermetic Limits
entries.summary: States that the vital faculty is beyond Hermetic magic, so spells cannot restore fatigue, reverse old age or revive a corpse, and notes the debate over whether this is part of the Limit of the Divine.
quotes: Affecting the vital faculty is beyond the power of Hermetic magic.

entries.title: Limits of Hermetic Magic: Knowledge, Reading and Translation
entries.summary: States what Hermetic magic cannot do with knowledge: it cannot create or transfer inscribed memories, Intellego does not cover the meaning of information, and no spell can read or translate written words because they have no mind behind them.
quotes: A magus cannot create knowledge using magic, and can only manipulate it indirectly.
There is, for example, a profound lack of a spell that can translate the written word from one language to another

entries.title: Spell Mastery
entries.summary: Each Formulaic or Ritual spell has a mastery Ability that adds to casting score and subtracts botch dice, and mastered spells are always cast with a stress die but with no botch dice when relaxed.
quotes: MASTERY ABILITY: Adds to casting score and subtracts from number of botch dice
If a maga has a score of one or greater in a mastery ability, she is said to have mastered that spell.

entries.title: Mastered Spell Special Abilities
entries.summary: Each level of a mastery Ability grants one special ability that applies only to that mastered spell.
quotes: For every level in the Mastery Ability, the maga may also choose one special ability, which applies only to that mastered spell.

versions.title: Mastered Spell Special Abilities (Access Rules)
versions.requires: Taught by someone who has the Ability (true lineage magi)
versions.summary: New spell mastery special abilities can be chosen when a level in mastery is earned, provided part of the experience was taught by someone with that Ability; characters taking Mastered Spells at creation may spend mastery points on them if they had access during apprenticeship.
quotes: as long as some of the experience points were taught by someone with the Ability

entries.title: Mastery: Adaptive Casting
entries.summary: A mastery score and its special abilities may be applied to similar spells, using only one mastery Ability's score and abilities per casting.
quotes: You may use your mastery score and all the special abilities associated with it whenever you cast a similar spell

entries.title: Mastery: Ceremonial Casting
entries.summary: Allows ceremonial casting rules for a mastered spell, but not for Ritual spells.
quotes: This special ability may not be taken for Ritual spells, as they effectively use ceremonial casting to start with.

entries.title: Mastery: Fast Casting
entries.summary: Allows a mastered Formulaic spell to be fast-cast by the Spontaneous fast-casting rules, with mastery offsetting the botch dice; not available for Rituals.
quotes: The maga may Fast Cast the mastered spell according to the rules for Fast Casting Spontaneous spells

entries.title: Mastery: Imperturbable Casting
entries.summary: Adds the Mastery score to Concentration rolls related to the spell.
quotes: Add the caster's Mastery score to all Concentration rolls related to the spell.

entries.title: Mastery: Magic Resistance
entries.summary: Doubles the caster's Magic Resistance against the mastered spell and similar spells or powers.
quotes: Your Magic Resistance is doubled against the mastered spell

entries.title: Mastery: Multiple Casting
entries.summary: Allows casting several copies of a mastered spell at once, up to the Mastery score in extra copies, each rolled separately with aiming penalties; usable for Rituals at extra vis cost.
quotes: You may cast a number of additional copies of the spell equal to or less than your Mastery Score.
AIMING: Penalty of one for every separate target, including the first

entries.title: Mastery: Obfuscated Casting
entries.summary: Others cannot automatically identify the spell's Form and must add the caster's Mastery score to the Ease Factor to work it out.
quotes: must add the caster's Mastery score to the Ease Factor

entries.title: Mastery: Penetration
entries.summary: Adds the Mastery score to the Penetration Ability score when determining the Penetration Bonus.
quotes: The maga's Mastery Score is added to her Penetration Ability score for determining her Penetration Bonus

entries.title: Mastery: Precise Casting
entries.summary: Adds a bonus to Finesse rolls with the spell (including aiming) and removes a botch die; can be taken multiple times.
quotes: Add +1 to all Finesse rolls the caster makes with the spell, including aiming rolls.

entries.title: Mastery: Quick Casting
entries.summary: Adds a bonus to Initiative Total (and to Fast Casting Speed) when casting the mastered spell; cannot be taken for Rituals.
quotes: Add +1 to the caster's Initiative Total when he casts the mastered spell.

entries.title: Mastery: Quiet Casting
entries.summary: Reduces the penalty for casting quietly; taken twice it allows silent casting without penalty.
quotes: The penalty for casting a spell quietly is reduced by five.

entries.title: Mastery: Rebuttal
entries.summary: For Muto or Rego Vim spells that affect another being's magic, adds three times the Mastery score to the effective level.
quotes: The magus may add three times his Mastery score to the effective level of the Vim spell

entries.title: Mastery: Still Casting
entries.summary: Allows casting the mastered spell without gestures at no penalty.
quotes: The maga can cast the spell without gestures, at no penalty.

entries.title: Mastery: Unravelling
entries.summary: For Perdo Vim spells that weaken or destroy magic, adds three times the Mastery score to the effective level.
quotes: The magus may add three times his Mastery score to the effective level of the Perdo Vim spell

entries.title: Books on Spell Mastery
entries.summary: A spell Mastery book can be studied by anyone who knows an identical spell, and the reader may learn any special ability, not only those of the author.
quotes: two spells are the same if they have the same Arts, level, Range, Duration, Target, and effect

entries.title: Spell Mastery Special Abilities
entries.summary: New Spell Mastery special abilities: Imperturbable Casting, Obfuscated Casting, Precise Casting and Quick Casting.
quotes: Add +1 to the caster's Initiative Total when he casts the Mastered spell.

entries.title: Spell Mastery for Urban Characters
entries.summary: Points out which Spell Mastery abilities help urban magi and mentions a form of mastery that lets formulaic spells use ceremonial casting bonuses without any initiation.

entries.title: Spell Levels and Magnitudes
entries.summary: Defines a spell's level as its base level from the guideline plus adjustments for Range, Duration, Target and size, and explains magnitudes (level divided by five, rounded up), which also give the vis cost of a ritual.
quotes: The magnitude of a spell is equal to one fifth of its level, rounded up.
the number of pawns of vis needed to cast a ritual spell
SPELL MAGNITUDE: Level/5 (rounded up)

entries.title: Level Guidelines
entries.summary: Explains that the guidelines give the lowest level at which a Ritual, Formulaic or Spontaneous spell can produce an effect, using the lowest Range, Duration and Target as the baseline.
quotes: the range of the spell is Personal, the duration is Momentary, and the target is Individual.

entries.title: Ritual Spells
entries.summary: Lists what only Ritual spells can do or must be Ritual: Year Duration, Boundary Target, levels above the Formulaic limit, lasting Momentary Creo creations, and effects the troupe judges too spectacular. Rituals have a minimum level and cannot be replicated spontaneously.
quotes: Ritual spells are always at least level 20, even if the level calculation would make them lower.
Formulaic and Spontaneous spells may not have a level greater than 50.
It is never possible to replicate the effects of a Ritual spell with Spontaneous magic, even when casting Ceremonially.

entries.title: Requisites
entries.summary: Explains requisite Arts: those needed for the effect add no levels, those that add an effect add at least a magnitude. A requisite limits the casting score to the lower of it and the primary Art, and requisites never change Magic Resistance or vis matching.
quotes: REQUISITE NECESSARY FOR SPELL'S EFFECT: +0 magnitudes
REQUISITE ENHANCES SPELL'S EFFECT: +1 magnitude or more
ADDED EFFECT IS PURELY COSMETIC: No requisite

entries.title: How to Read a Spell (Technique and Form)
entries.summary: Explains how spells are presented (grouped by Form then Technique), that guideline Range, Duration and Target default to Personal, Momentary and Individual unless noted, and the two-letter abbreviation style such as CrIg 15.
quotes: If the guideline does not specify a Range, Duration, or Target, they are Personal, Momentary, and Individual.

entries.title: Spell Damage
entries.summary: Spell damage written as +X means a stress die plus X, rolled anew each casting, which the target resists with Soak Total plus a stress die.
quotes: This is an abbreviation for stress die + X.
The target resists this damage with their Soak Total + stress die.

related.text: ArM5 Combat chapter, damage and Soak

entries.title: The Central Rule of Spell Design
entries.summary: The troupe may always override the guideline system and set a higher or lower level for an odd combination of Range, Duration, Target and effect; storyguides should not let the system force things past common sense.
quotes: The troupe may always intervene and declare that a certain combination of Range, Duration, Target, and effect warrants a higher or lower level than that described by the guidelines and the system below.

entries.title: Casting Requisites
entries.summary: Casting requisites are chosen at casting time rather than listed with the spell; the lowest Technique and Form among the primary and chosen requisite Arts is used for the Casting Total.

entries.title: Spontaneous Requisites
entries.summary: Requisites limit the Arts of Spontaneous spells in the same way as Formulaic ones.

entries.title: General Level Spells
entries.summary: General (Gen) spells can be learned at any level; the level at which you know one is where you learned or invented it, it cannot be used above or below that level, and each level is a different spell.
quotes: General level spells are open-ended only in the sense that they may be learned at any level.

entries.title: Spell Design Line
entries.summary: Describes the parenthetical calculation at the end of each spell: base level in levels plus modifications in magnitudes, with the reminder that a magnitude is one level up to level five.

entries.title: The Lyceum on Substance and Categories
entries.summary: Goes through Aristotle's ten categories and says which of them Hermetic Techniques currently affect, which are indirect, and which would need a new Technique or a breakthrough. Useful guidance when adjudicating or inventing unusual effects.
quotes: Changes in continuous quantity are under the control of Muto; such changes are rarely natural.

entries.title: Causality and Spell Design
entries.summary: Uses Aristotelian causes to decide which Hermetic Form a spell that imitates a natural phenomenon belongs to: the target is the material cause and magic replaces the efficient cause.
quotes: The target of Hermetic magic is always the material cause of the spell, and so the correct Hermetic Form can be determined by considering that which is changed.

entries.title: Consequences of Generation and Destruction (Creo and Perdo)
entries.summary: Explains what Creo can and cannot create (only things that can exist as natural forms, healing as restoring a form) and why Perdo dissolves substance rather than improving it.
quotes: Further, Creo magic cannot cause a cat to grow wings, because wings are not part of the form of a cat, but it can restore a leg which has been removed.
Perdo magic dissolves substances, not matter.

entries.title: Consequences of Alteration (Rego and Muto)
entries.summary: Distinguishes natural alteration, which is handled by Rego, from Muto, which changes categories of quality without changing substance. Includes the implications for shapechanging and Bjornaer heartbeasts.
quotes: Alteration does not necessarily fall under the Hermetic Technique of Muto; in fact, most alteration is in terms of natural changes, and is the purview of Rego spells.

entries.title: Consequences of Growth and Diminution (Creo and Muto)
entries.summary: Says growth is best simulated with Creo, while Muto growth changes the category of quantity and cannot be permanent.
quotes: Growth is most easily simulated with magic by creating more substance directly by informing new matter to account for the change in size, and thus is an exercise of the Technique of Creo.

entries.title: Consequences of Motion (Rego, Penetration and Aiming)
entries.summary: Explains why thrown missiles do no extra damage for speed, why objects guided by Rego are affected by Magic Resistance, and the two ways a Rego spell can avoid needing Penetration, each of which requires an Aiming roll.
quotes: This method requires an Aiming roll to ensure the object is released in the right position.

related.text: Houses of Hermes: Societates, House Flambeau

entries.title: Generating Worms (Rego Animal vermin)
entries.summary: Describes how Rego Animal spells can produce vermin from suitable raw substrate, how many creatures a Target: Group spell yields, and the cap on creatures per standard individual of the substrate.
quotes: a Target: Group spell is capable of producing a mass of animals equal to 10 standard targets (animals of Size +1)
can produce a maximum of 1000 creatures regardless of their size

entries.title: Ranges, Durations, Targets (overview)
entries.summary: Introduces the three spell parameters and their ordering by difficulty. Spontaneous spells must use the standard categories, while Formulaic and Ritual spells may be invented with non-standard ones at troupe discretion.
quotes: The Range governs how far the target can be from the magus, the Duration determines how long the target will be affected, and the Target describes what the spell can affect.

entries.title: Changing Ranges, Durations and Targets
entries.summary: Shows how to calculate a spell's level when its Range, Duration or Target is raised or lowered from the base, a magnitude per step, with a special rule that below level five a magnitude is a single level. Includes a worked example.
quotes: add one magnitude (five levels) to the level of the spell for every step by which the parameter is raised
Below level 5, adding a magnitude only adds one level, and subtracting a magnitude only subtracts one level.

entries.title: Range, Duration and Target Table
entries.summary: Table ranking every Range, Duration, Object, Container and Sense target by the additional magnitudes it adds to a guideline.

entries.title: Spell Ranges
entries.summary: Describes each Range (Personal, Touch, Eye, Voice, Sight, Arcane Connection): how distance to the nearest part of the target is measured, how far a voice carries, what eye contact requires, and how continuing spells behave if the caster moves away.
quotes: The range of a spell is the distance to the nearest part of the target of the spell.
Typically, firm words carry about 15 paces, while quiet words are audible within 5 paces and a shout carries about 50.

entries.title: Spell Durations
entries.summary: Describes each Duration (Momentary, Concentration, Diameter, Sun, Ring, Moon, Year), what happens to momentary effects under longer durations, recasting a spell to keep it continuous, and the rules for drawing a Ring.
quotes: In the absence of distractions, assume that a magus can concentrate for fifteen minutes per point of Concentration ability.
A spell with this duration must be ritual.

related.text: ArM5 p.215 Hermetic Magic chapter, concentration rules

entries.title: Spell Targets
entries.summary: Describes the object, container and sense Targets (Individual, Circle, Part, Group, Room, Structure, Boundary), what each can affect, and which require Ritual casting.
quotes: There are three types of target: objects, containers, and senses.
A spell with this target must be a Ritual.

entries.title: Targets and Sizes
entries.summary: Target types depend on kind of thing not size, but the size of the target affects spell level in every Form except Intellego and Circle targets: each magnitude added multiplies the allowed mass or volume. Gives the base Part, Group, Room, Structure and Boundary sizes, and how to adjust for enlarging or shrinking.
quotes: Adding one magnitude (five levels) to the spell multiplies the maximum size of its target by ten.
A base Room is large enough to fit a hundred standard Individuals with some squashing.
Mass of ten standard Individuals

entries.title: Magical Senses
entries.summary: Intellego spells can grant a magical sense (Taste, Touch, Smell, Hearing, Vision) as a Target; the information is limited like the mundane sense, must penetrate Magic Resistance, and one spell grants only one sense.
quotes: A single spell grants a single magical sense.

entries.title: Magical Wards
entries.summary: Rego wards protect the thing targeted from things of a Form; Circle wards bar crossing in both directions, are usually Ring Duration, and must Penetrate and equal or beat the Might of what they hold off.
quotes: because a ward with these parameters wards against creatures with a Might equal to or less than its level

entries.title: Static and Dynamic Container Targets
entries.summary: Spells with container Targets either affect what is inside at the moment of casting (static) or whatever is inside throughout the duration (dynamic); this is fixed when the spell is designed and gives two different spells.
quotes: This is the way that spells with object Targets work, and can be referred to as a static target
This can be referred to as a dynamic target, because the things that are targeted by the spell can change over the duration.

entries.title: Being Inside a Container
entries.summary: Uses an intuitive definition of what counts as inside a Circle, Room, Structure or Boundary, with examples, and lets the troupe be more precise if needed.

entries.title: Persistence of Containers
entries.summary: Explains when a container target still exists for a spell (same container, moved, resized, rebuilt) and why Circles and bare-marker Boundaries are vulnerable to being broken or altered.

entries.title: Targets and Creo
entries.summary: A Creo spell's Target is the thing created, always Individual or Group; creating a part of something is healing or Muto, and filling a room needs a Group target with a size modifier.
quotes: The target of a Creo spell that actually creates something is the thing created.

entries.title: Volumes and Targets
entries.summary: Reference list of volumes in tenfold steps, each equal to one magnitude of size, matched to base Individuals for several Forms and to the Material and Size table.

related.text: ArM5 p.255 Material and Size table

entries.title: Spells in Church
entries.summary: For Hermetic spells, explains how a church is divided into Rooms (nave, tower floors, a petitioned-off chancel) and that the whole church can be targeted as a Structure.
quotes: For Hermetic magic, the nave and each floor of the tower count as separate Rooms.

related.text: ArM5 Ch.4 Target Room and Structure

entries.title: Spells to Affect a Parish
entries.summary: Gives the Boundary-target Size Modifiers needed for Hermetic spells to cover a typical rural parish, urban parish or whole diocese, provided the borders are clearly defined.
quotes: A rural parish of typical size requires a spell with a Boundary target, with a +4 Size Modifier.

entries.title: Sigils
entries.summary: Every maga has a wizard's sigil that appears in her spells and enchantments, never needing requisites and never useful or crippling, and a separate voting sigil for Tribunal.
quotes: Whatever the form of the sigil, it never requires requisites, as it is part of the maga's magic.

entries.title: The Wizard's Sigil
entries.summary: A magus's personal quirk that shows up in the spells they invent and identifies the caster; it does not usually change effectiveness, and learned spells still carry your own sigil.
quotes: it is always your sigil that manifests in your spells.

related.text: ArM5 p.224 Hermetic Magic chapter, sigils

entries.title: Spell Traces and Sigils
entries.summary: Rules of thumb for how the magnitude of a spell trace decays over time, how long traces remain detectable, and how a caster's sigil can be revealed and recognized by Intellego Vim investigation.
quotes: As soon as the magic finishes, the magnitude halves.
A spell trace is normally detectable until it reaches a magnitude of –10, at which point it is completely gone.

entries.title: Shroud Magic
entries.summary: Explains how the Shroud Magic spell replaces a spell trace's sigil with a false one, how a magus can try to mimic another magus's sigil with an embedded Ease Factor, and how observers can test it.
quotes: Intelligence + Finesse + Stress die
Perception + Awareness + Stress die

entries.title: Creo Vim Guidelines (Refreshing Spell Traces)
entries.summary: A general Creo Vim guideline for refreshing spell traces within the target back to a fresh state, limited by the guideline's magnitude.
quotes: Refreshes all spell traces within the target that are less then the magnitude of the guideline

entries.title: Intellego Vim Guidelines (Detecting Magic Traces)
entries.summary: General guidelines for detecting spell traces of negative magnitude, with a higher magnitude step revealing rough details, the caster's sigil and whether a spell or an invested device produced the effect. Separate spells are needed for each of the four Realms.
quotes: Detect the traces of magic of negative magnitude up to the magnitude of the guideline used

entries.title: Identifying a Magus by Sigil
entries.summary: Once a caster's sigil has been detected in spell traces, an investigator familiar with that Tribunal's magi can recognise whose it is with an Intelligence plus Organization Lore roll, which is harder for an unfamiliar investigator.
quotes: make an Intelligence + Organization Lore: Order of Hermes roll against an Ease Factor of 9 (or 15 if the investigator is unfamiliar with Rhine magi)

entries.title: Detecting Spell Traces
entries.summary: When a spell's Duration ends it leaves traces whose strength fades over time at rates depending on the original Duration. Investigators can detect them with Intellego Vim effects whose level scales with the trace strength, and extra magnitudes reveal the Form, Technique and even the caster's sigil.
quotes: When a spell's Duration expires it leaves behind spell traces equal to half the magnitude of the original spell.
Traces down to magnitude zero can be detected by a base InVi 10 effect.

entries.title: Animal: How It Works
entries.summary: What Animal magic covers and the boundary with Mentem and Corpus: creatures with Cunning are affected by Animal in the mind, those with Intelligence need Mentem. Covers shapechangers, Bjornaer in animal form, animal parts on humans, and the base Individual.
quotes: If the creature has Intelligence, a Mentem spell must be used. If it has Cunning, an Animal spell must be used.
A basic Individual for Animal is an animal of about the same size as a pony, Size +1 or lower.

entries.title: Creo Animal Notes
entries.summary: Notes on creating animals and animal products: treated and processed products cost extra magnitudes, created animals just act naturally unless a Rego requisite is added, and Personal range is rarely usable.
quotes: Most Animal spells cannot be used with Personal range, so the level of a spell must be higher than the guidelines given.

entries.title: Perdo Animal Notes
entries.summary: Perdo Animal causes damage directly, so there is normally no Soak against it and only Magic Resistance defends.
quotes: There is normally no Soak against Perdo Animal

entries.title: Aquam: How It Works
entries.summary: What Aquam affects (water and other liquids, but not liquids that are part of a body without special design), how target categories apply to bodies of liquid, and base Individual sizes for water, natural, processed and corrosive liquids and poisons.
quotes: A base Individual for Aquam is a pool of water about five paces (fifteen feet) across, and two paces deep at the center.

entries.title: Creo Aquam Notes
entries.summary: Created water only quenches thirst temporarily; unnatural liquids cost extra magnitudes and need Muto requisites; poisons created have a base Ease Factor that rises with each magnitude.
quotes: Poisons created at the guideline level have an Ease Factor of 3. Each magnitude added to the level of the spell adds 3 to the Ease Factor.

entries.title: Muto Aquam Notes
entries.summary: Liquids inside a body can only be transformed by a spell designed for it with a Corpus or Animal requisite; poisons made by Muto use the same Ease Factor scaling as Creo Aquam.
quotes: Poisons created at the guideline level have an Ease Factor of 3. For every magnitude added to the spell, add three to the Ease Factor.

entries.title: Rego Aquam Notes
entries.summary: Rego Aquam can turn water to ice or steam; slightly or very unnatural controlled movement costs extra magnitudes.
quotes: Rego Aquam can change water into ice or steam, because these are both states that water can have naturally.

entries.title: Auram: How It Works
entries.summary: Auram covers air and most weather; explains how Individual and Group apply to weather phenomena and gives the base Individual as a phenomenon affecting a Boundary-sized area.
quotes: A base Individual for Auram is a weather phenomenon that affects the area within a standard Boundary

entries.title: Creo Auram Notes
entries.summary: Weather is normally created at Sight range because it begins in the upper air; ground-level weather is unnatural and its extra cost cancels the saving from shorter range.
quotes: Weather phenomena are normally created at Sight range.

entries.title: Rego Auram Notes
entries.summary: Rego Auram controls existing weather, including starting and stopping rain, but cannot create a breeze; precise or powerful control raises the magnitude.
quotes: It is not possible to create a breeze with Rego Auram, but it is possible to direct the course of a storm.

entries.title: Corpus: How It Works
entries.summary: Corpus affects human and humanlike bodies, including many faeries, and the base Individual is an adult human.
quotes: A base Individual for Corpus is an adult human being, up to Size +1.

entries.title: Perdo Corpus Notes
entries.summary: Perdo Corpus harm is often permanent unless repaired by other magic; diseases inflicted by magic have a base Ease Factor that rises with each magnitude and cannot be reduced by lowering level.
quotes: Diseases caused by magic have a base Ease Factor of 6. For every magnitude by which the spell level increases, the Ease Factor increases by 1.

entries.title: Rego Corpus Notes
entries.summary: Rego Corpus can perform surgery; detailed surgical rules are in another book.
quotes: Rego Corpus can be used to perform surgery.

entries.title: Herbam: How It Works
entries.summary: Herbam covers living and dead plants and plant matter including wood, and its base Individual is a plant about a pace in each direction.
quotes: A base Individual for Herbam is a plant roughly one pace in each direction.

entries.title: Creo Herbam Notes
entries.summary: Created food is nutritious only if the spell is a Ritual; plants can be created living or dead; treated and processed plant products cost extra magnitudes; one spell creates one type of plant product.
quotes: Any food created is nutritious only if the creation is a Ritual.

entries.title: Ignem: How It Works
entries.summary: Ignem covers fire, light and heat (including cold as absence of heat); warns that botches should be deadly, and gives the base Individual as a large campfire.
quotes: The base Individual for Ignem is a large campfire or the fire in the hearth of a great hall.

entries.title: Muto Ignem Notes
entries.summary: More intense fires are harder to change: spell level rises with the fire's damage above a threshold.
quotes: For every five points by which the fire's damage exceeds +5, add one magnitude to the level of the spell.

entries.title: Perdo Ignem Notes
entries.summary: More intense fires are harder to destroy: spell level rises with the fire's damage above a threshold; botches may create fire or freeze the caster.
quotes: For every five points by which the fire's damage exceeds +5, add one magnitude to the level of the spell.

entries.title: Rego Ignem Notes
entries.summary: More intense fires are harder to control, with a magnitude added for each step of fire damage above a threshold; Rego Ignem also controls heat and light.
quotes: Rego Ignem spells can control heat or light as well as fire.

entries.title: Imaginem: How It Works
entries.summary: Imaginem affects images and sensations rather than light or minds: how beasts, demons, faeries and the Church react to illusions, and a Perception + Finesse stress roll with Ease Factors to mimic specific objects or people.
quotes: It is more difficult to mimic a specific object or person using an Imaginem spell than it is to mimic a general image, and requires a Perception + Finesse stress roll.

For mimicking people, a roll against an Ease Factor of 6 lets you fool acquaintances of the person, an Ease Factor of 9 lets you fool friends, and an Ease Factor of 12 lets you fool close friends and relatives.

entries.title: Creo Imaginem Notes
entries.summary: Creo Imaginem makes only images, not the things themselves (an image bucket holds no water); extra complexity, movement, intelligible speech or intricacy add magnitudes.
quotes: Creo Imaginem spells only create the images of things, not the things themselves.

entries.title: Intellego Imaginem Notes
entries.summary: Intellego Imaginem detects real images at a distance; it needs light or sound at the place observed, and each extra sense perceived adds a magnitude.
quotes: each additional sense you wish to perceive increases the level of the spell by one magnitude

entries.title: Muto Imaginem Notes
entries.summary: Muto Imaginem alters existing images and persists without concentration; mimicking a specific voice or face needs familiarity and acquaintances may see through it; Imaginem cannot overcome the Gift.
quotes: Muto Imaginem, or indeed other Imaginem magic, cannot overcome the effects of The Gift, although it might offset them a little.

entries.title: Perdo Imaginem Notes
entries.summary: Perdo Imaginem dulls the senses an object affects (including invisibility); destroying changing images costs more, Momentary duration only makes an object flicker, shadows are Ignem not Imaginem, and mirror images follow the changed species.
quotes: Destroying something's shadow is thus Creo Ignem, or possibly Rego Ignem, not Perdo Imaginem.

entries.title: Rego Imaginem Notes
entries.summary: Rego Imaginem displaces where an image appears to be; changing images and images that change with the object cost extra magnitudes, as does each additional sense.
quotes: Add one level of magnitude to the guidelines for each additional sense to be affected.

entries.title: Mentem: How It Works
entries.summary: Mentem governs intelligent minds, thoughts, emotions, memories and the mental Characteristics; beasts need Animal magic. Minds have no size so size modifiers do not apply to Individual targets, but Groups and containers scale as normal.
quotes: Minds do not have a size, so size modifiers do not apply to Mentem effects with Individual targets.

entries.title: Intellego Mentem Notes
entries.summary: A Momentary Intellego Mentem spell can answer a single question, however complex the feeling, but not why; writing is not Mentem (it is Animal and Herbam or Terram), so translation needs a reader.
quotes: In general, a momentary Mentem spell can answer a single question, although it is not necessary that the answer be expressible in a brief form.

entries.title: Muto Mentem Notes
entries.summary: Muto Mentem covers changed memories, unnatural thoughts and emotions, and making a mind physical. Also explains how to grant a magical sense to many people at once, using Muto Mentem with Intellego and Form requisites.
quotes: granting a magical sense to multiple people is a function of Muto Mentem.

entries.title: Perdo Mentem Notes
entries.summary: Destroyed emotions return naturally so need a continuing Duration; destroyed memories stay gone with Momentary Duration unless a continuing spell prevents relearning.
quotes: Emotions naturally reappear in a person, so spells that destroy them must have a continuing duration to ensure that they do not come back.

entries.title: Terram: How It Works
entries.summary: Terram covers earth, stone, clay, metal, glass and many inanimate objects. It lists materials in order of difficulty and gives base Individual sizes that depend on the material.
quotes: it is harder to affect certain materials: Here, in increasing order of difficulty, are the materials Terram spells affect: earth (sand, dirt, mud), clay, stone, glass, metal, gemstones.

entries.title: Creo Terram Notes
entries.summary: Creating earth in an elaborate shape, or with an unnatural property and a Muto requisite, costs an extra magnitude; botches can entomb the caster.
quotes: Creating earth in an elaborate shape or, with a Muto requisite, with some unnatural property is one level of magnitude higher than the listed guidelines.

entries.title: Muto Terram Notes
entries.summary: Guidelines assume dirt; changing to or from stone or glass, or metal or gemstone, adds magnitudes once, and the amount changed is limited by the base Individual at each end.
quotes: To change to or from stone or glass, add one level of magnitude. To change to or from metal or gemstone, add two levels of magnitude.

entries.title: Perdo Terram Notes
entries.summary: Guidelines assume dirt; destroying stone or glass adds a magnitude and metal or gemstone adds more; botches can destroy the ground under the caster or metal they hold.
quotes: To destroy stone or glass, add one magnitude. To destroy metal or gemstone, add two magnitudes.

entries.title: Rego Terram Notes
entries.summary: Guidelines assume dirt; controlling stone or glass adds a magnitude and metal or gemstones add two, except when simply moving an item, and very precise manipulation costs more.
quotes: Add one magnitude to control stone or glass, and two for metal or gemstones, unless the item is simply being moved from one place to another

entries.title: Vim: How It Works
entries.summary: How Vim magic works: it acts on spells, magical effects, spirits and demons, most Vim spells are General level and their guidelines relate the Vim spell's level to the level of the target, with modified Range or Target costing power. Spells and effects have no size.
quotes: Most Vim spells are of General level, because the magic that Vim spells affect varies widely in power.

entries.title: Intellego Vim: Detecting Magic and Spell Residues
entries.summary: How magic detection works: the base level gives rough strength within a magnitude, extra magnitudes reveal realm, Arts, and details; items need a season in the lab to investigate; residues of spells halve and then decay over time; creatures and raw vis are detected by dedicated spells.
quotes: Investigation requires that you spend at least one season in the laboratory to discover what magic an enchanted item contains
As soon as the magic finishes, the magnitude halves.
A 'negative magnitude' of 10 indicates that the residue has disappeared completely, and no longer exists to be detected.

entries.title: Muto Vim: Changing Other Spells
entries.summary: Rules for meta-magic that alters other Hermetic spells: not usable on Spontaneous spells, needs an Intelligence + Concentration roll when you cast both, timing and Penetration against another magus' spell, Duration at least as long as the target casting, and Ritual requirements.
quotes: you must make an Intelligence + Concentration roll against an Ease Factor of 9 if you are casting both spells
It is not possible, for reasons that Hermetic theorists do not well understand, to use Muto Vim to affect another spell after it has been cast.

entries.title: Muto Vim Spells and Enchanted Devices
entries.summary: When a Muto Vim effect may be put into a magic item, and how to use or counter one against a device's effect: cooperation and timing, fast casting, beating Penetration, and identifying the Form.
quotes: The caster must succeed with an Intelligence + Concentration roll against an Ease Factor of 9.

related.text: ArM5 p.217 Determining Form of Magical Effect

entries.title: The Human Mind and the five inner wits
entries.summary: Describes the five inner wits (common sense, imagination, cognition, estimation, memory) and the soul's reason and intellect. This is the model that the extended Mentem guidelines in this chapter are built on.
quotes: The functions of the sensitive faculty — collectively called the inner wits — are the five components of the mind.

entries.title: The Hermetic Art of Mentem
entries.summary: Explains how the existing Mentem spell guidelines map onto the five inner wits, which are easier to affect, and that Hermetic magic cannot touch reason or intellect directly.
quotes: Broadly speaking, an existing guideline that mentions emotions is operating on the estimation, and a guideline that mentions thoughts is operating on the imagination.

related.text: The Mysteries Revised Edition pp.102-113 (dream spells)

entries.title: Magic Affecting Conscience (removing a demon's Obsession)
entries.summary: Sparking a target's conscience with Creo Mentem can strip a demon's Obsession Trait but cannot change existing Personality Traits. Includes the new level 10 Creo Mentem guideline for it.
quotes: Level 10: Spark a twinge of conscience in an intelligent being's mind, overriding the temporary obsession of a demon.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Infernal pp.31-32 (obsession power)

entries.title: Species
entries.summary: Describes the four kinds of species (iconic, echoic, haptic, olfactory and gustative) that Imaginem magic manipulates and which sense each one reaches.

entries.title: Species Magic: New Targets for Species
entries.summary: Explains how Muto spells treat species as a slightly unnatural substance requiring an Imaginem requisite, and defines the Individual, Part and Group Targets used for species, with an example spell.
quotes: The following Targets are used for species, supplementing those found in the core rulebook.

entries.title: Additional, Minor Senses
entries.summary: Describes proprioception, balance and pain as internal senses that Mentem can target and Corpus can attack, and says how they count for base spell levels.
quotes: Pain, proprioception and balance are treated as mental capabilities with regard to base levels for spellcasting given in the core rulebook.

entries.title: Mimicry: Making Illusionary Objects
entries.summary: Describes mimicry, the standard Hermetic illusion that sheds natural, non-magical species of a created object, needing little Finesse and not being resisted by the Parma Magica.
quotes: Mimics are not resisted by the Parma Magica, because their species are not magical.

entries.title: Transparency (Destroying Species Before They Reach a Viewer)
entries.summary: Rules for illusions of transparency that hide an object from one viewer: the base level, the Individual Target used, the Perception + Finesse roll and a table of Ease Factor modifiers by size of the hidden object.
quotes: Casting an illusion of transparency requires a Perception + Finesse roll against an Ease Factor of 6.
Transparencies use the Individual Target to represent the stream of species between the hidden object and observer.

entries.title: Macrotures: Illusions of Proximity to the Organ of Perception
entries.summary: Describes macrotures, images magnified beyond what the eye can do by forcing species to strike the eye less concentrated, and the uses magi find for them.
quotes: These are already discussed in the Intellego Imaginem guidelines in ArM5 (base level 3).

entries.title: Synaesthesia: Switching Organs of Perception
entries.summary: Explains synaesthetic illusions that alter species so a stronger sense perceives them, the limit that external-sense species changed into internal-sense ones have no effect, and the base level for such transformations.
quotes: Spells that transform the species that trigger one sense into those that trigger another have a base level of 2.

entries.title: Anamorphs
entries.summary: Rules for shapeless illusions that exploit the viewer's tendency to fill in details: a Perception + Awareness roll for the victim against a computed Ease Factor, a table of outcomes by margin, the base level, and the penalty for fooling extra senses.
quotes: Victim's Perception Ease Factor: die + value of dominant, active Personality Trait + caster's Perception + caster's Finesse
As images that affect a single sense, they have a base level of 1.

entries.title: Anamorph Example
entries.summary: A worked example of the anamorph rules showing how the victim's Ease Factor is totalled and how the guard's Perception + Awareness result is read.

entries.title: Miniatures: Tricks Using Perspective
entries.summary: Rules for miniatures, small illusions that send species in one direction to fake a larger scene or fool a single viewer: the extra magnitude, the Perception + Finesse roll, and a table of Ease Factor modifiers.
quotes: Most miniatures are one magnitude higher than the base level given by the table on page 144 of ArM5.
A miniature's caster must make a Perception + Finesse roll against an Ease Factor of 9 to successfully create the illusion.

entries.title: Memory
entries.summary: Introduces inscribed, procedural and episodic memories and what Hermetic magic can and cannot do with each, including that Abilities cannot be created by magic and episodic memories may give facts or a Lore success.
quotes: The core rulebook assigns a base level of 5 to spells that create a single memory.

entries.title: Procedural Memories
entries.summary: Procedural memories are the sequences behind physical Abilities used without thought; Hermetic magic can target but not create them, and rare inherited procedural memory is modelled with Virtues.
quotes: Hermetic magic may target procedural memories, but cannot create them.

entries.title: Episodic Memories
entries.summary: Describes episodic memories and gives the Intelligence + Finesse roll that sets how detailed and convincing a created episodic memory is, with results from botch to success by 9 or more.
quotes: The level of detail in an episodic memory is dependent on an Intelligence + Finesse roll against an Ease Factor of 6.

entries.title: The Memorization of Created Knowledge
entries.summary: Explains how a target can retain a created thought or memory after the spell expires by using it to build episodic memories, and the time that takes and its imprecision.
quotes: This is not an effective teaching aid, because it requires an hour of work for each image or significant cluster of facts to fix itself in memory.

entries.title: Other Tricks of Memory (Storage and Inclinations)
entries.summary: Gives spell guidelines for turning a memory or emotion into a solid object and for Rego Mentem inclinations such as belief or lack of interest.
quotes: The base level of this is 5, and it requires a Requisite for the final form of the memory.

entries.title: New Rego Animal Guideline (vermin)
entries.summary: New Rego Animal spell guideline for causing vermin to generate spontaneously, with a note on when a requisite for the substrate is needed.
quotes: Cause vermin to spontaneously generate in appropriate matter, such as flesh, plants, soil, or water.

entries.title: Creo Mentem Guidelines (inner wits)
entries.summary: Extends the Creo Mentem guidelines to show which inner wit each affects, including hallucinations in the common sense, planted thoughts and emotions, and dreams or plans in cognition.
quotes: Additional species cost one magnitude each

versions.title: Creo Mentem Guidelines (Restoring Memories)
versions.summary: New Creo Mentem guidelines for restoring a fragment of a memory to a fresh state, at levels scaled to how much time the memory covers.
quotes: Level 5: Restore a memory of an event to a fresh state, as long as a fragment of it remains.

entries.title: Intellego Mentem Guidelines (inner wits)
entries.summary: Extends the Intellego Mentem guidelines to read emotions, senses, surface thoughts, memories, short-term plans, and dreams through the relevant wit.
quotes: interrogates the imagination, and can also be used to read the entire common sense

entries.title: Muto Mentem Guidelines (inner wits)
entries.summary: Extends the Muto Mentem guidelines so changes to memories, emotions and rewriting a mind can alter imagination, estimation, common sense and cognition.
quotes: can rewrite any of the five wits

entries.title: Perdo Mentem Guidelines (inner wits)
entries.summary: Extends the Perdo Mentem guidelines to the five wits, noting that damage to wits other than memory heals naturally.
quotes: Unlike memories, destroyed aspects of the imagination, cognition, common sense, and estimation naturally restore themselves.

entries.title: Rego Mentem Guidelines (inner wits)
entries.summary: Extends the Rego Mentem guidelines to control emotions, thoughts, dream subject and content, and complex commands through the relevant wit.
quotes: directly controls the cognition, setting the target's goals towards that determined by the caster.

entries.title: Intellego Terram Guidelines (Commune with Stone and Metal)
entries.summary: New Intellego Terram guidelines for communing with the spirit of a natural rock, an artificial rock or a metal object, at progressively higher levels.
quotes: Level 30: Commune with a natural rock. Speak with a metal object.

related.text: Dream of the Mind That Sits

entries.title: Perdo Vim Guidelines (Aging Traces and Dispelling Enchantments)
entries.summary: Guidelines for aging a spell trace to a negative magnitude and for ritual dispelling of Hermetic enchantments, either generally or of one specific type such as Talismans, Familiars or Longevity Rituals.
quotes: Gen: Ages a spell trace to a negative magnitude equal to the guideline used.

entries.title: Creo Aquam Guidelines
entries.summary: New Creo Aquam guideline for creating ice in natural shapes.
quotes: Create ice in a natural shape, such as a floe or icicle.

entries.title: Muto Auram Guidelines
entries.summary: New Muto Auram guidelines for turning a gas into a harmful gas that causes a Light or Medium Wound.
quotes: Transform a gas into a harmful gas causing a Light Wound (Stamina roll against Ease Factor 6 to resist)

entries.title: Perdo Terram Guidelines
entries.summary: New Perdo Terram guideline for destroying a single aspect of dirt.
quotes: Destroy one aspect of dirt, such as its weight or its cohesiveness

entries.title: Rego Terram Guidelines
entries.summary: New Rego Terram guidelines for throwing stone projectiles, with damage limited by spell level.
quotes: Hurl a stone projectile with enough force to do +5 damage (range increment of 20 paces)

entries.title: Created Emotional Bias
entries.summary: Guidelines for spells that cloud a mind with emotion as an artificial Personality Trait, how extreme and milder emotions are resisted, and base levels for directed, undirected and class-directed emotions.
quotes: Spells that create extreme emotions can be resisted with a roll of any opposed Personality Trait against an Ease Factor of 9.
Spells that create milder emotions are resisted by a roll against an Ease Factor of (4 + the score of the artificial Personality Trait)

related.text: ArM5 p.148 Panic of the Trembling Heart

entries.title: Diminished Mental Capability
entries.summary: Extends the Perdo Mentem guideline for destroying a mental capacity with a list of other capacities a spell can inhibit.
quotes: This has a base level of 4, noted on page 150 of ArM5.

related.text: ArM5 p.150 Trust of Childlike Faith

entries.title: States of Consciousness
entries.summary: Guideline for Rego Mentem spells that alter a target's mental state, with a list of further states (animalist, anaesthetic, daydreaming, dreaming, self-aware, somnambulistic, unconscious) that can be targeted like the core examples.
quotes: These spells have a base level of 4 (ArM5, page 151).

entries.title: Altering Thoughts
entries.summary: Explains that Mentem magic can target thoughts or the capacity to think, and that changing or destroying thoughts uses the same base levels as for memories.
quotes: It is also possible to change and destroy thoughts, using the same base levels as for memories.

related.text: ArM5 p.150 Tip of the Tongue

entries.title: New Corpus Guidelines
entries.summary: A new Creo Corpus spell guideline for improving all of a target's wounds at once.
quotes: Level 25: Improve all wounds by one level of severity.

entries.title: Ward Guidelines
entries.summary: Spell guidelines for wards in each Form, all at Touch range, Ring duration and Circle target. Used to set levels for Hermetic ward spells and for the Warding Ability.
quotes: All of them are presented at Range Touch, Duration Ring, and Target: Circle
Ward against human beings. (Touch, Ring, Circle)

entries.title: New Spell Guideline: Rego Vim
entries.summary: A Rego Vim guideline for sustaining or suppressing spells of a specific type cast by another, limited by the level of the Vim spell.
quotes: Sustain or suppress a spell or spells of a specific type cast by another with level less than or equal to the level + 2 magnitudes of the Vim spell

entries.title: New Perdo Corpus Guidelines (Energy Magic)
entries.summary: Guidelines for lengthening Short-Term Fatigue recovery, causing loss of Short-Term or Long-Term Fatigue, and preventing recovery by rest.
quotes: Level 5: Cause a target to lose a Short-Term Fatigue level.

entries.title: New Creo Corpus Guidelines (Energy Magic)
entries.summary: Guidelines for speeding Fatigue recovery and restoring Short-Term or Long-Term Fatigue levels; only Momentary Ritual effects truly restore, while other Durations cause the levels to return as Long-Term Fatigue loss.
quotes: Ritual spells formulated according to these guidelines with Momentary Duration truly restore Fatigue levels.
Level 15: Restore a lost Long-Term Fatigue level.

entries.title: New Spell Guidelines for Auras
entries.summary: Introduces new Intellego Vim and Rego Vim guidelines for detecting tethers and suppressing auras, usable by any maga who has studied at least one of Conciatta's unpublished works.

entries.title: New Intellego Vim Guidelines (tether detection)
entries.summary: Spell guideline levels for detecting the presence and strength of natural or supernatural tethers (the sources that feed an aura) and for detecting subsumed auras.
quotes: Detect the presence and strength of a supernatural tether of level 5 or higher.
Detect the presence of a subsumed aura.

related.text: Realms of Power: Magic p.10 tethers

entries.title: New Rego Vim Guidelines (suppressing auras)
entries.summary: A general Ritual guideline for suppressing an aura up to a given strength for the spell's duration, and what happens if the aura later grows beyond the ritual's power.
quotes: Suppress an aura of strength less than or equal to the spell's magnitude.

entries.title: Spells to Summon and Command Spirits (guidelines)
entries.summary: Reprints the Rego Mentem guidelines for controlling and summoning a disembodied spirit of a given Form.
quotes: Control a disembodied spirit of (Form).
Summon a disembodied spirit of (Form).

entries.title: Rego Vim Guidelines (activating enchanted devices)
entries.summary: New Rego Vim guideline letting a spell trigger an enchanted device that has a simple trigger, provided the caster knows the triggering action; linked and environmental triggers are excluded.
quotes: Activate an enchanted device with a simple trigger (i.e., not a linked trigger or an environmental trigger, see

entries.title: New Spirit Spells and Spell Guidelines
entries.summary: General rule that spells to summon, perceive or control spirits must penetrate the spirit's Magic Might, with notes on controlling a Daimon's Aspect.
quotes: All spells to summon, perceive, or control a spirit must penetrate its Magic Might.

entries.title: Intellego (Form) Spirit Guidelines
entries.summary: Intellego guidelines for sensing supernatural creatures whose Might is aligned to a Form, graded by minimum Might.
quotes: Sense a supernatural creature of Might 30 or above with a Might associated with the Form.

entries.title: Rego (Form) Spirit Guidelines
entries.summary: Rego guidelines for controlling and summoning Airy Spirits tied to a Form; an Arcane Connection is always needed to summon.
quotes: Control an Airy Spirit of (Form).
Summon an Airy Spirit of (Form).

entries.title: Rego Vim Spirit Guidelines
entries.summary: Rego Vim guidelines for controlling or summoning Airy Spirits of a Realm, and a general guideline for summoning a Daimon's Aspect as a Ritual.
quotes: Summon an Aspect of a Daimon if (level + 4 magnitudes) equals or exceeds twice its Might. (Ritual)

entries.title: Apotropaic Guidelines
entries.summary: Sidebar of new Vim spell guidelines for dealing with demons: restoring Might, creating Arcane Connections, speaking with, binding, weakening, commanding and summoning them.
quotes: Restore a demon's Might Pool by (the level of the spell + 10), as long as the spell penetrates its Magic Resistance.
Reduce the Casting Total for a specific type of magic (such as Infernal Powers) cast by the target by the (level + 2 magnitudes) of the spell.

entries.title: New Creo Herbam guidelines (healing plants)
entries.summary: Adds Creo Herbam guidelines for healing wounds, disease and poison in plants, and notes that non-Momentary healing spells suspend rather than complete healing, as for Creo Corpus.
quotes: Like Creo Corpus healing spells, a healing spell cast other than as a Momentary Duration Ritual actually suspends the healing process

entries.title: New Spell Guidelines: Rego Herbam (Plant Disease Wards)
entries.summary: New Rego Herbam guidelines for wards that protect plants against mundane or realm-linked magical plant diseases, using a Touch, Ring, Circle format.
quotes: Ward a plant against mundane plant diseases.

entries.title: New Spell Guidelines: Creo Herbam (Healing Plants)
entries.summary: New Creo Herbam guidelines for healing plant wounds and curing plant diseases by severity, with a note that plant disease severity mirrors the disease in the eater and that non-Momentary healing is suspended like Creo Corpus healing.
quotes: Cure a Critical plant disease
Heal all damage to a plant, including wounds, disease, and poison.

entries.title: New Spell Guidelines: Creo Animal (Animal Diseases)
entries.summary: New Creo Animal guidelines for curing animal diseases by severity, with a general base to stop any disease, and the same suspended-healing caveat as Creo Corpus healing.
quotes: Stop the progress of any disease. Cure any disease countering its effects.

entries.title: Making Naphtha With Magic
entries.summary: Spell guideline for creating naphtha with Creo Aquam, giving the Base level and Base Individual size, and noting that it ignites if made outside a container.
quotes: This gives Creo Aquam spells a Base level of 3, and the Base Individual target is a pool one foot across and six inches deep, regardless of the viscosity of the naphtha.

entries.title: Consumption Guidelines
entries.summary: General notes on victims and targets for Consumption effects, including extra magnitudes for animals and plants and the need to penetrate Magic Resistance.
quotes: the effect must penetrate it to have any effect on the target

entries.title: Debauchery/Consumption guidelines
